Context: I’m about to graduate college and am completely unemployed. My lease ends at the end of the summer so I have a few months to get my life together. What I’d like to do is pick a city, get an apartment in that city, move there, and get a job being a barista or lifeguard, etc, just a small job to pay the rent while I figure out what I want to do with my life. I’ve seen studio apartments online for about $500-800, which seems pretty reasonable, but I’m completely overwhelmed by the leasing process, how to pick which city to move to, what parts of that city to avoid, etc. I think most places even require you to have a job before they’ll let you sign your lease. Any advice? Anything vaguely related to this situation would be helpful :) Thanks!
How do you move to a new city?

What's your financial situation? Unemployed is a minor obstacle to renting if you can offer to pay a few months in advance.

I'd estimate if you have $5000 or more saved, you can probably do as you propose; less than that and you'll have to secure a job offer first.
First find out where the work is that you went to school for then pick a city .
Once you figure out which city, you can start with registering an account on city-data.com and ask questions. The people are snobby but knowledgeable.
Save up, buy a class B RV, go wherever you want.

Step 1. Pick a date. This is the date you move. Step 2. Find a place to crash while you look for apartments, or find a cheap apartment with a six month lease. Your roommates will probably be assholes. Step 3. Save enough money to live there for a couple of months while you find a job (it shouldn't take that long). Step 4. Move on the date that you picked.

That's the most bare bones way to move I can think of. I moved to NYC from Tennessee with no marketable skills when I was younger, and those are the steps that I followed, and my move was more or less successful (I did burn through my first two months rent getting an 18 foot u-haul through the Lincoln Tunnel, but I found a job quickly).

Good luck on your move. It really is as simple as picking a date, finding a place to live, and being on the ball about job hunting when you get there.

One often overlooked thing about moving to a new city, especially if you are single is that there is no support system. In Short, if you have no friends or family, it could very well suck and you could be miserable. I don't mean to imply that this is always the case, but it is something the many people don't even consider.

Also, make sure your field has good openings in that area. I am in Application Development and I live in a great city for it. I would absolutely LOVE to move to Montana, but lets face it, there aren't a lot of opportunities in the AppDev field up there.

Get the job before you move, but have an idea about where to stay before you accept.

If you get a job and no place to stay, and its a larger city, you can often rent a room at an extended stay motel or something. These will be more expensive than an apartment, generally, but don't require a lease, deposit, etc. It might work until you get a month or 6 weeks under your belt and can find a place.

If you have friends or family, pay them (up front) for a room for a month or so.

Once you have a job and a place, then its just a matter of making it work, but you have to do that no matter where you live.
